claim.pdf_says: First data row of the EXAMPLE 3 table. Initial Value of ITEM cell reads 'BBEABDABABBCABE' with a wrapped continuation 'E' on the next line - one 16-character value, BBEABDABABBCABEE. Final Value of ITEM cell reads 'BBEXYZXYXYZCABV' with a wrapped continuation 'E' - one 16-character value, BBEXYZXYXYZCABVE.
claim.why_it_matters: The cell wrap was re-joined with a space instead of being closed up, so both COBOL data values now carry a spurious embedded space and read as 17 characters. Anyone lifting this INSPECT example as a test vector gets the wrong operand and the wrong expected result. That the true length is 16 is confirmed by the replacement: FIRST "E" BY "V" AFTER "D" turns character 15 into V and leaves character 16 as E, exactly as printed.

verdict.reasoning:
CONFIRMED on independent inspection of the 300-dpi render of PDF page 1182 (printed folio 1152) and of E:/Temp/specrecon/v1182/page-1182.md line 23.

GLYPHS AS PRINTED. I cropped the first data row of the EXAMPLE 3 table and read it at 2x. The 'Initial Value of ITEM' cell is set on two lines with NO intervening space glyph and no hyphen: line 1 'BBEABDABABBCABE' (15 characters, filling the cell to its right rule), line 2 'E' alone at the left of the same cell. The 'Final Value of ITEM' cell is identical in shape: line 1 'BBEXYZXYXYZCABV' (15 characters, again running to the cell edge), line 2 'E'. This is ordinary cell-width overflow of a single unbroken token, not two tokens. Every other row in the table (ADDDDC, ADDDDA, CDDDDC, BDBBBDB and their finals) is short enough to fit on one line and is transcribed correctly, which is exactly the pattern of a width-driven wrap.

TRANSCRIPTION. The markdown re-joins the wrap with U+0020: '| BBEABDABABBCABE E | 3 | 0 | 2 | BBEXYZXYXYZCABV E |'. Both quotes in the claim are exact - I diffed them character-for-character against the file.

WHY THIS IS NOT MERE LINE-WRAP FORMATTING (the usual grounds for rejection). Joining a wrapped line with a space is the correct default for prose, and I would reject it there. Here the wrap falls inside an indivisible alphanumeric data value, and the space character is itself a legal COBOL alphanumeric character. The injected space is therefore indistinguishable from data: the reader sees a 17-character operand containing a blank in position 16 rather than the 16-character operand ISO printed. The character content of a normative example changed; that is content, not presentation.

INDEPENDENT CONFIRMATION THAT THE TRUE LENGTH IS 16. I re-derived the whole row from the two INSPECT statements printed above the table on the same page, and the arithmetic only closes for the 16-character no-space value BBEABDABABBCABEE:
  - COUNT-0 FOR ALL "AB" BEFORE "BC": first 'BC' is at positions 11-12, so the region is 1..10; 'AB' occurs at 4-5, 7-8, 9-10 = 3. Table prints 3.
  - COUNT-1 FOR LEADING "B" AFTER "D": 'D' is at 6, position 7 is 'A', so no leading B = 0. Table prints 0.
  - COUNT-2 FOR CHARACTERS AFTER "A" BEFORE "C": region 5..11; positions 5, 7-8, 9-10 are already taken by the higher-precedence ALL "AB" clause in the single left-to-right scan, leaving 6 ('D') and 11 ('B') = 2. Table prints 2.
  - REPLACING: ALL "AB" BY "XY" BEFORE "BC" gives 4-5, 7-8, 9-10 -> XY; CHARACTERS BY "Z" AFTER "A" BEFORE "C" gives 6 and 11 -> Z; LEADING "B" BY "W" AFTER "D" fires nowhere; FIRST "E" BY "V" AFTER "D" turns position 15 into V and leaves position 16 as E. Result BBEXYZXYXYZCABVE - character-for-character the printed final value.
A 17-character operand with a blank at position 16 would push the trailing E to position 17 and would not reproduce COUNT-2 = 2 or the printed final value. The claim's stated rationale is therefore correct as well as its quotations.

I checked the rest of the page for the same defect and found none: the EXAMPLE 4 table (ABABABABC / 1 / ABABXYABC) fits on one line and is clean, the two code blocks match the PDF line for line, and the header cells ('Initial Value' / 'of ITEM') are a genuine two-word phrase where the space-join is right.
verdict.corrected_description: Confirmed as described; only the severity label is arguably understated. Page 1182 (printed folio 1152), EXAMPLE 3 table, first data row. The PDF sets each of the two 16-character ITEM values across two lines purely because of cell width - 'BBEABDABABBCABE' + 'E' and 'BBEXYZXYXYZCABV' + 'E', with no space or hyphen glyph at the break. The markdown (page-1182.md line 23) re-joins each wrap with a space, yielding 'BBEABDABABBCABE E' and 'BBEXYZXYXYZCABV E'. Correct transcription closes the wrap up: '| BBEABDABABBCABEE | 3 | 0 | 2 | BBEXYZXYXYZCABVE |'. Because a space is a valid alphanumeric character, this is a corrupted 17-character data value rather than a formatting artifact, and it silently breaks the example as an INSPECT test vector (both the operand and the expected result); I would classify it minor/content rather than cosmetic. The remaining four rows of the table and the EXAMPLE 4 table are transcribed correctly.
